translation_notes: self._namespace is a runtime instance attribute (a Namespace built from CLASSIC_CDF_NAMESPACE elsewhere in the class), not a value known at transpile time, so `@prefix classic: <{self._namespace}> .` is rejected: 'prefixe non declare' (checked interactively: @prefix only accepts a literal IRI, never an expression). Every classic: term (Relationship, sourceType, targetType, and the source_type/target_type values) had to be interpolated instead of written under a prefix -- a real limitation for any query built against a namespace that is only known at run time, worth confirming against ldpy/012 if not already listed there.

The query text itself (self._instances, a class attribute built with str.format placeholders) is defined OUTSIDE this extracted region/context; it was recovered from upstream (cognitedata/neat@4042d3e96) to translate faithfully rather than invented.

Cannot be driven to a verdict: `python -m ldpy` on translated.ldpy fails at the first external import (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cognite'), and original.py fails identically. Even with cognite.neat installed, _edge_triples calls self._relationship_as_edge (a DESCRIBE query + _create_edge, not part of the extracted region) and remove_instance_ids_in_batch (graph.commit()) plus a lookup_entity_with_external_id closure built by a sibling static method -- reconstructing all of that as a shim would mean re-authoring most of the RelationshipAsEdgeTransformer class rather than a minimal context shim, and risks exactly the 'verdict prouve seulement la transpilation' pitfall the batch was warned about.
